builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL
summary: The approach replaces single-shot prompting of LLMs for low-resource enterprise DSLs with an execution-graded loop in which the model compiles its output, receives errors, and edits iteratively, supplemented by carefully worded domain guidance. Costs are additional inference calls per task (higher token spend and latency), plus engineering effort to build the compile-feedback harness and to author and tune skill documentation; the paper also shows packaging guidance as a live plugin can halve its value (28% as documentation versus 14% as a plugin) unless the skill wording is rewritten. Failure modes include the loop not recovering from fundamental knowledge gaps (all models scored 0% on authoring from scratch), sensitivity to how guidance is phrased and delivered, and results that may not transfer beyond the proprietary Salesforce AgentScript setting in which they were measured.
rationale: The compile-and-edit loop is cheap to implement on constrained infrastructure and workload-agnostic in principle, but the evidence comes from a single proprietary DSL benchmark, so the reader should validate the gain on their own target language and task mix before adopting it in production.
technique: Agentic compile-and-edit loop for DSL code generation
